    Amor Fati

    🌿 Budding planted Feb 14, 2024 tended May 11, 2026
    #budding#stoicism#philosophy

    Amor fati — "love of fate." Not resignation, not gritted-teeth tolerance, but the active, almost greedy embrace of what is, including the parts you'd never have chosen.

    Nietzsche put it most aggressively:

    "My formula for greatness in a human being is amor fati: that one wants nothing to be different, not forward, not backward, not in all eternity. Not merely to bear what is necessary... but to love it."

    The relationship to control #

    This is the next move after The Dichotomy of Control. The dichotomy gets you to accept what isn't up to you — to stop spending energy on it. Amor fati asks for something harder: to welcome it. The difference is the difference between a patient tolerating weather and a sailor who's glad of the wind, whatever direction it's blowing, because wind is what makes sailing possible.

    Acceptance is subtraction (stop suffering). Amor fati is addition (start using).

    Where I actually use it #

    Mostly with failure, the engineering kind. A production incident is not up to me once it's happening; the dichotomy says: don't waste energy wishing it weren't. Amor fati goes further: this outage is the most honest teacher I'll get this quarter. The duplicate-charge bug that taught me Idempotency Is a Superpower was, genuinely, a gift. I would not give it back.

    It also shows up in the garden — the literal one. A late frost kills the seedlings; Three Sisters Planting fails; you don't curse the frost, you learn the frost date and plant a week later next year. The frost is not up to you. Loving the lesson is.

    The honest caveat #

    I find amor fati easy to write about and hard to do, especially in the first ten minutes of something going wrong. It's aspirational, which is why this note is still 🌿 budding and not evergreen. The dichotomy I can do on a bad day. The loving part I'm still practicing.
